subject: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

Team —

Following product's readiness check-in last week, Acme confirmed they want to flip the feature flag and do a staged production pilot on Dec 1. They expect a peaked window during the first 3 hours after GA where traffic will be ~4.2k requests/minute with avg 320 tokens per request (model: redwood/opt-13B-v1). Attached is the customer traffic model (acme_traffic_model_v2.csv) with minute-by-minute projections and a simple ramp plan (0 -> 30% -> 70% -> 100% over 3 hours).

Ask: we need a temporary quota/rate-limit exception and a short runway for a capacity guardrail (requested window: 2026-12-01 09:00 PST -> 2026-12-01 18:00 PST). Specifically:
- Increase tokens/min throughput to 80M tokens/min for the window
- Raise concurrent streaming connections to 650
- Provide a soft throttling band with a 2xx fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency crosses 600ms P95

Please confirm technical feasibility and what we need from Sales/CS (contracts/entitlements) to approve the exception. We need ops confirmation by EOD 11/30 to keep the Dec 1 pilot on track.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_traffic_model_v2.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

Thanks Marissa — good detail, appreciate the CSV. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I take this to Capacity:
- Burst profile: is that 4.2k RPM sustained for the full 3-hour window or are there minute-by-minute spikes above that in the sheet? (I see some short spikes to ~5k in the CSV but want confirmation)
- What percent of requests will be streaming vs non-streaming? If streaming > 30%, we need different connection headroom planning.
- Target latency SLOs? You mentioned P95 600ms threshold, confirm what we should treat as hard vs soft (i.e., automatic fallback).

Operationally I can submit the quota exception form (attaching quota_exception_request_form.pdf) but I need explicit ramp schedule from the customer and a signed entitlement (we can accept an email acknowledgement from the AC and follow up with a formal amendment after). Can we get the customer's minute-by-minute ramp and a short runbook for rollback steps?

Prelim timeline: if I have answers within 2 hours, I'll escalate to Capacity and ask for a temporary exception window limited to Dec 1 (auto-revoke at end). Otherwise we push the pilot.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: quota_exception_request_form.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

Looping in deal context — Acme is in final pilot tranche for our marketplace integration. They signed the MSA and have approved the implementation work (deal ACME-PIPE-2026-45). They need confirmation from us at least 24 hours before pilot to keep their engineering calendar. If we can't commit to the window they will move to the following week.

Notes for approvals: any temporary capacity exception will be billed at overage rates per contract; if Ops needs a formal entitlement change (commit), I can route a 30-day credit against usage to reduce friction. Let me know if you need a short approval email from Acme (I can get that).

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Sam Tillotson <sam.tillotson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

Thanks team — confirmed on our side. Short answers:
- The CSV reflects our expected minute-by-minute traffic. We will have three ramp phases on Dec 1:
  09:00-10:00 PST -> 0% to 30% (approx 1.2k RPM peak)
  10:00-12:00 PST -> 30% to 70% (approx 3k RPM peak)
  12:00-12:30 PST -> 70% to 100% (approx 4.2k RPM peak)
- Streaming ratio: ~22% (most calls are short response text generation)
- If latency rises above 600ms P95 we will gate at the feature flag and throttle on our side, but we prefer the platform fallback you suggested as a safety net.

I've attached our short prod-runbook excerpt with rollback steps and contact points (prod_runbook_excerpt.md). We'll provide the signed one-line acknowledgement email once you confirm the temporary window.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

I reviewed the traffic model and the numbers look achievable with a few constraints and a fallback plan. Technical notes:
- We can provision a temporary tokens/min increase to 80M for the window, but we need to pin model variants to avoid costly reloads. Propose: default -> redwood/opt-13B-v1-INT8-quant (lower mem) as the fallback.
- Set runtime connection headroom to 800 concurrent sockets (we'll reserve 150 for control-plane overhead).
- Enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompt contexts (will reduce effective token load by ~12% per the attached model).
- We should run a short 15-minute staged smoke at 09:15 PST to validate routing and autoscaler behavior. Ops needs a contact loop between our on-call and Acme's eng lead (Sam listed above).

If Ops confirms the exception, I will bake the fallback variant and pre-warm weights at 07:00 PST. Otherwise we will not pre-warm to avoid cost.

-Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Tillotson <sam.tillotson@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme pilot launch - quota escalation & forecast alignment

All —

Summary and decision: Capacity exception APPROVED for Acme pilot for a limited window on 2026-12-01 09:00 PST -> 2026-12-01 18:00 PST. Conditions and configuration below:
- Temporary quotas applied: tokens/min = 80,000,000; connection limit = 800 (150 reserved for control-plane).
- Runtime guardrail: fallback to redwood/opt-13B-v1-INT8-quant if P95 latency > 600ms for two consecutive 5-minute buckets.
- Autoscaler pre-warm: Rishi will pre-warm weights at 07:00 PST (confirmed).
- Operational runbook: follow prod_runbook_excerpt.md from Acme. Ops will run a 15-min smoke at 09:15 PST and will monitor token usage, error rate, and P95 latency.
- Billing: Ben — mark as overage under ACME-PIPE-2026-45; Sales will issue an acknowledgement to be stored on the HubSpot deal.
- Auto-revoke: all temporary quotas will be revoked at 18:00 PST automatically; any extension requires a recorded exec approval.

Next steps: Ben to secure the one-line written acknowledgement from Acme (email or DocuSign); Marissa to own feature-flag gating timeline; Rishi to confirm pre-warm succeeded; Monica to standby on CS notifications. I'll be watching metrics and will authorize rollback if thresholds breach.

Thanks everyone — good collaboration.

-Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345; https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG
Attachments: quota_exception_request_form.pdf, prod_runbook_excerpt.md
